facts.fact: The garbhagriha is the sanctum that houses the main deity.
Nagara, Dravida and Vesara are the three main temple styles.
The Nagara tower is the shikhara; the Dravida tower is the vimana.
The gopuram is the gateway tower of a Dravida temple.
The Hoysaleswara temple at Halebidu is a Vesara example.
Kandariya Mahadeva at Khajuraho is a Nagara temple.
In Kalinga architecture the tower is the deula and the hall the jagamohana.
The Lingaraj temple was built by the Somavamsis (11th c.).
Konark was built by Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty (13th c.).
Colossal gopurams and Virupaksha at Hampi mark the Vijayanagara style.
A chaitya is a prayer hall with a stupa; a vihara is a monastery.
The Barabar caves were excavated in the Mauryan period for the Ajivikas.
The Lomas Rishi cave is the earliest rock-cut cave and copies timber architecture.
Ellora has Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments together.
The Kailasa temple at Ellora, the largest monolithic excavation, was built by Krishna I.
Ajanta was rediscovered in 1819 by John Smith.
Ajanta became a UNESCO site in 1983.
Elephanta is famous for the Trimurti of Shiva.
Badami has the earliest Brahmanical cave paintings.
The Great Chaitya at Karla (Cave 8) is the largest rock-cut chaitya.
The Gandhara school had a Greco-Roman style.
The Mathura school used indigenous red sandstone.
The Amaravati school carved white marble narrative reliefs.
The pottery sequence is OCP → PGW → NBPW.
A stupa has an anda, harmika, chhatra, vedika and toranas.
The Lion Capital of Sarnath is the national emblem.
Most Ashokan edicts are in Prakrit in the Brahmi script.
Indo-Islamic architecture replaced the trabeate with the arcuate method.
A curvilinear shikhara is NOT an Indo-Islamic feature.
Gol Gumbaz (Bijapur) is in the Deccani style.
Adhai Din Ka Jhopra reused temple material.
Mughal miniature painting reached its zenith under Jahangir.
Indo-Saracenic fused Indian domes and chhatris with European forms.
Le Corbusier planned Chandigarh.
Laurie Baker was the 'Architect of the Poor'.
Charles Correa designed the Jawahar Kala Kendra, Jaipur.
The Maratha Military Landscapes were inscribed in 2025.
The Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath (2026) is the latest Indian World Heritage Site.
The Lepakshi Veerabhadra temple (Vijayanagara) is famous for its hanging pillar.
Srisailam (Mallikarjuna) is a Dravidian temple of AP.
Kalyana mandapas were a feature of Vijayanagara temples (UPSC 2016).
Charminar (1591) is a Qutb Shahi monument.
The pradakshina path is the circumambulatory passage around the sanctum.
The antarala is the antechamber (vestibule) between the sanctum and the mandapa.
The vahana is the deity's mount, placed facing the sanctum (e.g. Nandi for Shiva).
The dhvaja stambha is the flagstaff set before the sanctum.
A Garuda stambha carries Garuda, the mount of Vishnu.
The amalaka is the ribbed stone disc crowning a Nagara shikhara.
The kalasha (kumbha) is the pot-shaped finial at the very top of the tower.
A panchayatana temple has a main shrine with four subsidiary shrines at the corners.
The jagati is the raised platform on which a temple stands.
A yajna kund is a sacred fire pit for rituals near the temple.
The simple curvilinear Nagara shikhara is the latina or rekha-prasada type.
The phamsana shikhara is broader and shorter, with stepped slabs rising in a gentle slope.
The valabhi type has a rectangular plan and a barrel-vaulted roof.
The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh (Lalitpur, UP; c. 500 CE, Gupta) is an early panchayatana temple with a shikhara.
The Bhitargaon temple (Kanpur) is a Gupta-age brick temple.
Temple 17 at Sanchi is an early flat-roofed Gupta temple.
The Khajuraho temples (Kandariya Mahadeva, Lakshmana) were built by the Chandelas, 10th–11th centuries.
The Modhera Sun Temple (Gujarat) was built by the Solanki king Bhima I (1026), with a stepped tank (Surya Kund).
The Dilwara Jain temples at Mount Abu began with the Vimal Vasahi (1031) of Vimal Shah, minister of Bhima I.
The present Kashi Vishwanath temple was rebuilt in 1780 by Ahilyabai Holkar.
Mahmud of Ghazni sacked the Somnath temple in 1026.
In Kalinga architecture the rekha deula is the tall curvilinear tower over the sanctum.
The pidha deula is the pyramidal, tiered roof of the jagamohana.
The khakhara deula is a barrel-roofed type (e.g. Vaital Deul, Bhubaneswar).
The natamandira is the dance hall in front of the jagamohana.
The Jagannath temple at Puri was built by Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva (12th century).
Konark is called the Black Pagoda; it is a stone chariot of the Sun with 24 wheels drawn by 7 horses.
The Rajarani temple (Bhubaneswar, 11th c.) has no deity in its sanctum.
The Mukteshwar temple (Bhubaneswar) with its torana arch is called the 'gem of Odishan architecture'.
Prakaras are the concentric enclosure walls of a Dravida temple.
A kalyana mandapa (hall for the deity's wedding) is typical of Vijayanagara temples.
The amman shrine is a separate shrine for the consort goddess, common from the Vijayanagara–Nayaka period.
Dvarapalas are the door-guardian figures at a Dravida temple entrance.
Mahendravarman I's Mandagapattu cave was the first Pallava rock-cut shrine, made without brick, timber, metal or mortar.
The Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram are monoliths of Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla), 7th century.
Arjuna's Penance (Descent of the Ganga) is a giant open-air rock relief at Mahabalipuram.
The structural Shore Temple and the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram were built by Rajasimha (Narasimhavarman II).
The Vaikuntha Perumal temple at Kanchipuram was built by Nandivarman II.
Rajaraja I completed the Brihadeeswarar (Rajarajeswaram) temple at Thanjavur in 1010.
The Gangaikondacholapuram temple was built by Rajendra I to mark his Ganga expedition.
The Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram was built by Rajaraja II.
Chola bronzes such as the Nataraja were cast by the lost-wax (cire perdue) process.
The Meenakshi temple at Madurai in its present form is a Nayaka work (17th c.), with a Hall of a Thousand Pillars.
The Ramanathaswamy temple, Rameswaram, has the longest temple corridor in India.
The Ranganathaswamy temple, Srirangam, has seven prakaras.
The Vittala temple at Hampi is famed for its stone chariot and musical pillars.
The Hazara Rama temple at Hampi, the royal chapel, carries Ramayana friezes.
The colossal gateways added by Krishnadevaraya are called raya gopurams.
Aihole is called the 'cradle of Indian temple architecture' (Lad Khan, Durga temple).
The Durga temple at Aihole has an apsidal (gajaprishtha) plan.
The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built by Queen Lokamahadevi to mark Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas.
At Pattadakal the Papanatha temple is in the Nagara mode beside Dravida temples.
The Badami cave temples were excavated under the Chalukya king Mangalesha.
Hoysala temples stand on a star-shaped (stellate) jagati and are carved in soapstone (chloritic schist).
The Chennakeshava temple at Belur was built by Vishnuvardhana in 1117.
Halebidu, site of the Hoysaleswara temple, was the Hoysala capital Dorasamudra.
The Keshava temple at Somanathapura (1268) is a late Hoysala work.
The Ramappa (Rudreshwara) temple at Palampet was built in 1213 by Recherla Rudra, general of Kakatiya Ganapatideva.
The Thousand Pillar temple at Hanamkonda was built by Kakatiya Rudradeva (1163).
The Navabrahma temples at Alampur (Badami Chalukya) carry Nagara shikharas in the far south.
The Bodhisattva Padmapani painting is in Ajanta Cave 1.
The later Ajanta caves were excavated under Vakataka patronage (Harishena, 5th c.).
Ellora is also called Verul Leni.
Indra Sabha and Jagannatha Sabha are the Jain caves at Ellora.
The Elephanta caves were cut in basalt; the site was Buddhist before becoming Shaivite.
The four Barabar caves are Lomas Rishi, Sudama, Vishwakarma and Karan Chaupar.
The Nagarjuni hill caves were dedicated to the Ajivikas by Ashoka's grandson Dasharatha.
The Bagh caves (MP, 6th c.) have earthy, secular paintings done in tempera.
The Nashik caves ('Pandav Leni') are 24 Hinayana Buddhist caves of the 1st century CE.
The Mandapeshwar cave (Borivali) was Brahmanical and later converted into a Christian shrine.
Bhaja has one of the earliest Buddhist chaityas of the Western Ghats.
Kanheri (Mumbai) has over a hundred Buddhist caves.
The Udayagiri caves near Vidisha (Chandragupta II) are famous for the Varaha relief.
The Udayagiri–Khandagiri caves (Odisha) are early Jain rock-cut shelters of Kharavela's time.
Guntupalli (Eluru district, AP) has a rare circular rock-cut Buddhist chaitya.
The Undavalli cave temple (Guntur district, Vishnukundin era) has a colossal reclining Vishnu (Anantasayana).
The Borra caves (Araku, AP) are natural limestone caves with stalactites and stalagmites.
The bronze Dancing Girl of Mohenjodaro was cast by the lost-wax process.
The bearded "priest-king" of Mohenjodaro is carved in steatite.
The Didarganj Yakshi (chauri-bearer) is a polished Mauryan sandstone figure.
A rock-cut elephant emerges from the rock at Dhauli (Odisha) beside an Ashokan edict.
The Gupta Sarnath school is known for Buddhas with transparent drapery and an ornate halo.
Ramkinkar Baij of Santiniketan was a pioneer of modern Indian sculpture.
Black and Red Ware is a Chalcolithic–megalithic pottery.
Red Polished Ware with stamped designs belongs to the Kushana period.
Blue pottery of Persian origin is the hallmark craft of Jaipur.
Major Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga war and Ashoka's remorse.
Major Rock Edict II names the southern kingdoms (Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputras, Keralaputras) and medical care for men and animals.
Major Rock Edict V records the appointment of Dhamma Mahamatras.
Major Rock Edict XII urges tolerance and respect among all sects.
The Rummindei pillar records Ashoka's visit to Lumbini and the village's tax relief.
The Nigali Sagar pillar records the enlarging of the stupa of Buddha Kanakamuni.
The Maski edict was the first found to name Ashoka ('Devanampiya Asoka').
Kalsi (Dehradun) has the complete set of 14 major rock edicts in north India.
The Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts are in the Kharoshthi script.
The Kandahar edict is bilingual in Greek and Aramaic.
The Sohgaura copper plate records famine relief in pre-Ashokan Brahmi.
The rust-free Mehrauli iron pillar celebrates King Chandra (Chandragupta II).
The Allahabad pillar carries Ashoka's edict, Harisena's prashasti of Samudragupta and Jahangir's inscription.
Ravikirti's Aihole inscription records Pulakeshin II's victory over Harsha.
Rudradaman's Junagadh (Girnar) inscription, the first long Sanskrit inscription, records repairs to the Sudarshana lake.
Gautami Balashri's Nasik inscription lists Gautamiputra Satakarni's victories.
The Hathigumpha inscription gives a year-by-year account of Kharavela.
The Besnagar Garuda pillar was set up by the Greek envoy Heliodorus in honour of Vasudeva.
The Bhattiprolu casket inscriptions (AP) are the earliest Brahmi records of south India.
Queen Naganika's Naneghat inscription records Satavahana Vedic sacrifices.
The Halmidi inscription (c. 450 CE) is the earliest Kannada record.
The Talagunda inscription tells the origin of the Kadambas under Mayurasharman.
The Kudumiyanmalai inscription (Pallava) records musical notation.
The Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I describe elections to Chola village assemblies.
The Gwalior inscription (c. 875) records Pratihara Mihira Bhoja.
The Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque (Delhi, Qutbuddin Aibak) is the oldest mosque in India, built from temple material.
The Qutub Minar was begun by Aibak and completed by Iltutmish.
The Alai Darwaza (1311) of Alauddin Khalji has the first true arch and dome in India.
Tughlaqabad fort and the tomb of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq have sloping (battered) walls.
The Hauz Khas complex has the madrasa of Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
The Khirki Masjid (Delhi) is named after its perforated windows.
The Atala Masjid of Jaunpur is a Sharqi monument.
Hoshang Shah's tomb at Mandu, the first marble tomb in India, is seen as a precursor of the Taj.
The Adina Mosque at Pandua (Bengal) is the largest mosque of the Bengal Sultanate.
The madrasa of Mahmud Gawan at Bidar is a Bahmani building.
The granite Mecca Masjid of Hyderabad was begun by the Qutb Shahis (1617) and completed under Aurangzeb (1694).
Golconda fort is noted for its acoustic system and diamond trade.
Humayun's tomb, built by Haji Begum and designed by Mirak Mirza Ghiyas, introduced the double dome and garden tomb.
The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri marks Akbar's victory over Gujarat.
The five-storeyed Panch Mahal stands at Fatehpur Sikri.
Itmad-ud-Daulah's tomb (Agra), built by Nur Jahan, is the 'Baby Taj' and first large use of pietra dura.
The chief architect of the Taj Mahal was Ustad Ahmad Lahori.
The Red Fort (Delhi) was built by Shah Jahan (completed 1648).
The Moti Masjid in Delhi's Red Fort is Aurangzeb's; the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort is Shah Jahan's.
Bibi ka Maqbara (Aurangabad), the tomb of Aurangzeb's wife, is the 'Taj of the Deccan'.
Safdarjung's tomb (Delhi) is the last great Mughal garden tomb.
The Bara Imambara (Lucknow), a famine-relief work of Asaf-ud-Daula, has a vast hall without beams.
Squinches and pendentives let a round dome sit on a square base.
Foreshortening made inscriptions placed high up appear the same size as those near the eye.
The six limbs of painting (shadanga) are listed in Vatsyayana's Kamasutra.
Bhimbetka has over 500 rock paintings, most of them Mesolithic.
Pala painting was Buddhist palm-leaf manuscript art (e.g. Ashtasahasrika Prajnaparamita).
The Apabhramsa (Western Indian) school illustrated Jain texts such as the Kalpasutra.
Akbar's atelier under Mir Sayyid Ali and Abd al-Samad produced the Hamzanama.
Ustad Mansur was Jahangir's master painter of birds and animals.
Kishangarh's Bani Thani (Nihal Chand) is called the 'Indian Mona Lisa'.
Basohli is the boldest-coloured Pahari school.
Kangra painting is famous for Gita Govinda themes.
The Deccani school produced Bijapur Ragamalas and Golconda royal portraits.
Abanindranath Tagore, leader of the Bengal School, painted 'Bharat Mata'.
The Progressive Artists' Group (1947) included F.N. Souza, M.F. Husain and S.H. Raza.
S.H. Raza is known for his 'Bindu' series.
Raja Ravi Varma (Kilimanoor, Travancore) popularised oil painting and mythological lithographs.
Kalighat painting of 19th-century Bengal was bold and satirical.
Warli painting (Maharashtra) uses white rice paste on mud walls.
Madhubani painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar.
Pattachitra is the cloth painting of Odisha, centred at Raghurajpur.
Phad is the scroll painting of Rajasthan (e.g. Pabuji).
Pichwai paintings of Nathdwara depict Krishna.
Gond art belongs to Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
Saura paintings are ritual wall art of Odisha.
Chittara is a Karnataka wall art on red backgrounds.
Sanjhi is a paper-cutting art of Uttar Pradesh (Mathura).
Cheriyal (Nakashi) scroll painting belongs to Telangana.
The Sé Cathedral of Goa (1619) houses the Golden Bell.
The Basilica of Bom Jesus (Goa, 1605) holds the relics of St Francis Xavier.
Diu Fort was built by the Portuguese in 1535.
French colonial buildings were 'faceless' — plain facades without ornament.
The Victoria Memorial (Kolkata, 1921) was designed by William Emerson.
The Gateway of India (1924), marking George V's visit, was designed by George Wittet.
Mumbai's CSMT (Victoria Terminus, 1887) was designed by F.W. Stevens.
The Chepauk Palace (Chennai) is regarded as the first Indo-Saracenic building.
Henry Irwin designed the Viceregal Lodge (Rashtrapati Niwas), Shimla (1888), and the Mysore Palace.
Lutyens' New Delhi was called the 'Rome of Hindustan'.
India Gate, the All-India War Memorial for First World War dead, was designed by Lutyens.
The circular Parliament House (1927) was designed by Herbert Baker.
The Supreme Court building (1958) was designed by Ganesh Bhikaji Deolalikar.
The IIM Ahmedabad campus was designed by Louis Kahn.
The Lotus Temple (Delhi, 1986), a Bahá'í house of worship, was designed by Fariborz Sahba.
The Neo-Dravidian Vidhana Soudha (Bengaluru, 1956) was the project of Chief Minister Kengal Hanumanthaiah.
The India Habitat Centre (Delhi) was designed by Joseph Allen Stein.
The Hall of Nations at Pragati Maidan was designed by Raj Rewal.
The Gandhi Smarak Sangrahalaya at Sabarmati (1963) is by Charles Correa.
Mumbai's Kanchanjunga Apartments are by Charles Correa.
Laurie Baker is also called the 'Gandhi of Indian Architecture'.
The National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad, was designed by Gautam Sarabhai.
The IIT Kanpur campus was designed by Achyut Kanvinde.
B.V. Doshi became the first Indian to win the Pritzker Prize (2018).
Agra Fort was inscribed in 1983.
The Taj Mahal was inscribed in 1983.
The Sun Temple, Konark, was inscribed in 1984.
The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram was inscribed in 1984.
The Churches and Convents of Goa were inscribed in 1986.
The Khajuraho Group of Monuments was inscribed in 1986.
The Group of Monuments at Hampi was inscribed in 1986.
Fatehpur Sikri was inscribed in 1986.
The Group of Monuments at Pattadakal was inscribed in 1987.
The Elephanta Caves were inscribed in 1987.
The Great Living Chola Temples were inscribed in 1987 (extended in 2004).
The Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi were inscribed in 1989.
Humayun's Tomb was inscribed in 1993.
The Qutb Minar and its Monuments were inscribed in 1993.
The Mountain Railways of India were inscribed in 1999 (Darjeeling), extended for Nilgiri (2005) and Kalka–Shimla (2008).
The Mahabodhi Temple Complex, Bodh Gaya, was inscribed in 2002.
The Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka were inscribed in 2003.
The Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park was inscribed in 2004.
Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (Mumbai) was inscribed in 2004.
The Red Fort Complex was inscribed in 2007.
The Jantar Mantar, Jaipur, was inscribed in 2010.
The Hill Forts of Rajasthan were inscribed in 2013.
Rani-ki-Vav (the Queen's Stepwell), Patan, was inscribed in 2014.
The Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara was inscribed in 2016.
Le Corbusier's Capitol Complex, Chandigarh, was inscribed in 2016 as part of a transnational site.
The Historic City of Ahmedabad, India's first World Heritage City, was inscribed in 2017.
The Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai were inscribed in 2018.
Jaipur City was inscribed in 2019.
The Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple, Telangana, was inscribed in 2021.
Dholavira, the Harappan city, was inscribed in 2021.
The Veerabhadra temple and monolithic Nandi of Lepakshi (AP) are on India's UNESCO Tentative List (2022).
